name: Stop sharing updates with other PCs
summary: Download Windows updates directly, with no peer uploads.
what: Sets the Delivery Optimization download mode to HTTP only with no peering.
benefit: Your connection is not used to upload update files to other PCs.
risk: None. Updates still download from Microsoft. Hidden on Home, which has no policy support. Use the setting in Windows Update advanced options there.
advice: Suggested if you do not want your connection used to serve updates to other PCs.
facts: Mode 0 means HTTP only with no peering
Documented in the vendor policy reference
Not available on Home, which has no policy support

name: Allow long file paths
summary: Let apps use paths longer than 260 characters.
what: Turns on the long path setting for the file system. Apps must also declare support.
benefit: Fewer path too long errors in developer tools and deep folder trees.
risk: None. Apps that do not declare support behave as before.
advice: Suggested for developers and anyone who sees path too long errors.
facts: Apps must also opt in through their manifest
Apps that do not opt in are unaffected
Documented by the vendor

name: Turn off Fast Startup
summary: Make Shut down a full shutdown.
what: Sets the hybrid boot value to 0 so the kernel session is not saved on shutdown.
benefit: Clears stale driver and update state, helps dual boot and some device issues.
risk: Low. Cold boot can take a few seconds longer, mostly on hard drives.
advice: Suggested if you dual boot, swap drives or fix odd issues with Restart but not Shut down. Skip it for the fastest cold boot.
facts: Shut down normally saves a kernel session to disk
Restart is already a full restart
Cold boot can take a few seconds longer

name: End task from the taskbar menu
summary: Add End task to the right-click menu of taskbar apps.
what: Turns on the developer setting that shows End task on taskbar items.
benefit: Kill a stuck app in two clicks without opening Task Manager.
risk: None. Unsaved work in the app is lost when you use it.
advice: Suggested for everyone. Handy for stuck apps.
facts: Windows 11 23H2 and later
It is a developer setting made visible
Unsaved work in that app is lost when you use it

name: Show hidden files
summary: Show files and folders marked hidden.
what: Sets the Explorer hidden file view option to show.
benefit: See folders like AppData without changing view options each time.
risk: None. Be careful deleting files you do not recognize.
advice: Suggested if you work with folders like AppData. Otherwise leave it off.
facts: Per account setting
Hidden system files stay protected and hidden
Take care deleting files you do not know

name: Open File Explorer to This PC
summary: Start in drives and folders instead of Home.
what: Sets the Explorer launch target to This PC.
benefit: Straight to your drives, no recent files list.
facts: Per account setting
Shows drives and folders instead of recent files
Takes effect the next time Explorer opens

name: Hide the Task View button
summary: Remove the Task View button from the taskbar.
what: Turns off the Task View taskbar button for the current user. Win+Tab still works.
facts: Win+Tab still opens Task View
Per account setting
Explorer restarts once to apply

name: Hide the taskbar search box
summary: Remove the search box or icon from the taskbar.
what: Sets the taskbar search mode to hidden. Search still opens from the Start menu.
facts: Search still opens from Start or Win+S
Per account setting
Takes effect immediately

name: Instant menus
summary: Open cascading menus without the short delay.
what: Sets the menu show delay to 0 milliseconds. The default is 400.
advice: Suggested if menus feel slow to you.
facts: The Windows default is 400 milliseconds
Per account setting
Sign out to apply

name: Turn off the Sticky Keys shortcut
summary: Stop the pop-up when Shift is pressed five times.
what: Clears the keyboard shortcut flag that launches the Sticky Keys prompt.
benefit: No interruptions in games and fast typing.
risk: None. Sticky Keys can still be turned on from Settings.
advice: Suggested for everyone who does not use Sticky Keys, especially gamers.
facts: The usual default flag value is 510
Setting 506 clears only the hotkey bit that opens the prompt
Sticky Keys can still be turned on in Settings
Sign out to apply
